import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocTable } from '../../storybook/helpers';
import * as AccordionStories from './Accordion.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ accordion" — Documentation / Usage · Style · Accessibility + Example frames. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/accordion-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={AccordionStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>An accordion is a vertical stack of collapsible sections that condenses long content into scannable headers.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.SingleExpand} />

<Controls of={AccordionStories.SingleExpand} />

# Usage

## Overview

An accordion condenses long content into scannable headers. Users reveal one or more panels on demand — which also means content stays hidden until they open it.

### Variants

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.SingleExpand} />

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.MultipleExpand} />

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Styles} />

Single- vs multiple-expand is behavior (`expandMode`), not a Figma variant. Bordered and Borderless are the Style variant.

### When to use

- To condense long content into scannable headers that users open on demand.
- For FAQ-style content, where users pick the questions they need.

### When not to use

- For primary navigation.
- For content users must read in full.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Header** — a heading element wrapping the trigger button; the whole row is the hit target.
2. **Title** — start-aligned label for the section.
3. **Icon** — chevron showing collapsed or expanded; decorative.
4. **Content panel** — revealed on expand.

### Alignment

The title is start-aligned and the icon end-aligned on the same row. The trigger spans the full header width.

### Placement

Items stack vertically at full width — never side by side. Spacing between items is consistent; borderless accordions rely on it as their only separator. Avoid nesting accordions; if you must, indent and limit to one level.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.DoDont} />

## Content

- **Title** — wrapped in a heading (h2–h4) that fits the page outline.
- **Panel content** — every collapsed panel shows its icon, so hidden content always has a visible cue.

## Behaviors

### States

Items start collapsed (Default). Activating the trigger toggles its own panel; in single-expand mode, opening a panel collapses the one that was open.

- **Default** — collapsed, resting.
- **Hover** — the header background shifts (`surface/bg/subtle`).
- **Focused** — 3px focus ring on the header; never suppressed.
- **Expanded** — panel visible, chevron rotated 180°.
- **Disabled** — dimmed, can't change state, skipped in tab order.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Disabled} />

### Interactions

**Mouse** — clicking anywhere in the header toggles the panel.

**Motion** — panels animate height and opacity (about 200ms, ease-out) and the chevron rotates 0° → 180° in sync. With prefers-reduced-motion, toggling is instant.

# Style

## Color

<DocTable
  head={['Style · State', 'Header fill', 'Title', 'Icon', 'Border']}
  rows={[
    ['Bordered · Default / Expanded', 'surface/bg/default', 'text/primary', 'icon/default', 'border/strong (bottom, 1px)'],
    ['Bordered · Hover', 'surface/bg/subtle', 'text/primary', 'icon/default', 'border/strong (bottom, 1px)'],
    ['Bordered · Focused', 'surface/bg/default', 'text/primary', 'icon/default', 'border/interactive/focus (3px)'],
    ['Bordered · Disabled', 'surface/bg/default', 'text/disabled', 'icon/subtle', 'border/strong (bottom, 1px)'],
    ['Borderless · Default / Expanded', 'surface/bg/default', 'text/primary', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['Borderless · Hover', 'surface/bg/subtle', 'text/primary', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['Borderless · Focused', 'surface/bg/default', 'text/primary', 'icon/default', 'border/interactive/focus (3px)'],
    ['Borderless · Disabled', 'surface/bg/default', 'text/disabled', 'icon/subtle', '—'],
  ]}
/>

Panel fill `surface/bg/default`; body text `text/secondary`.

## Typography

<DocTable head={['Element', 'Tokens', 'Rendered size']} plain={[2]} rows={[['Title', 'text-style/heading/xs/*', '14px'], ['Body', 'text-style/body/sm/*', '12px']]} />

## Structure

<DocTable
  head={['Property', 'Value']}
  rows={[['Header and panel padding (horizontal)', 'space/inset/md · 12'], ['Header and panel padding (vertical)', 'space/inset/sm · 8'], ['Chevron', 'Icon/nav/chevron-down/20 · 20px'], ['Item width', '360 (fixed)']]}
/>

## Variants & states

10 variants: Style (2) × State (5).

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focused state with a 3px ring on the header, on both styles.
- A chevron on every item, so collapsed panels always have a visible cue.
- A Disabled state for triggers that can't change.
- A full-width header, so the whole row is the hit target.

## Development considerations

- Wrap each trigger `<button>` in a heading (h2–h4). Never place the button outside the heading.
- Set `aria-expanded` on the trigger and `aria-controls` pointing to its panel.
- Give the panel `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the trigger; use the `hidden` attribute when collapsed.
- Mark the chevron `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Disabled triggers use `disabled` and are skipped in tab order.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion — remove height and rotation animation.

## Keyboard interactions

<DocTable
  head={['Key', 'Action']}
  plain={[1]}
  rows={[['Enter', 'Toggles the focused panel'], ['Space', 'Toggles the focused panel'], ['Tab', 'Moves between triggers'], ['↓', 'Moves focus to the next trigger'], ['↑', 'Moves focus to the previous trigger'], ['Home', 'Moves focus to the first trigger'], ['End', 'Moves focus to the last trigger']]}
/>

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Keyboard} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocTable } from '../../storybook/helpers';
import * as AvatarStories from './Avatar.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ avatar" — Documentation / Usage · Style · Accessibility. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/avatar-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={AvatarStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>An avatar represents a user or entity with an image, an icon or initials, optionally paired with a name and email.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Default} />

<Controls of={AvatarStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Overview

Avatars represent people and entities at a glance. Use AvatarGlyph on its own, or AvatarIdentity to pair it with a name, email and optional trailing icon.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.ContentTypes} />

### When to use

- To represent a person with their photo or initials.
- To represent a system account, bot or non-person entity — Icon type.
- To identify someone next to their name and email — AvatarIdentity.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Avatar** — an AvatarGlyph (image, icon or initials).
2. **Name** — the person's or entity's name.
3. **Email** (optional) — secondary line.
4. **Trailing icon** (optional) — e.g. a chevron for a menu.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Identity} />

### Sizes and colors

Derive an initials avatar's color from a hash of the user's name or ID, so the same person always gets the same color.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.ColorsAndSizes} />

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.DoDont} />

## Content

**Initials**

- First letter of the first and last name — Jane Doe → JD.
- If the initials don't fit, shrink the font to fit rather than clip.

**Image**

- Needs alt text that names the person.
- If the image fails to load, fall back to the icon (if configured), then to initials.

## Behaviors

### States

AvatarGlyph is static. AvatarIdentity has interactive states for when it opens a profile card or menu: Default, Hover (`surface/bg/subtle`), Focused (3px focus ring), Active (pressed), Selected (persistent highlight), Disabled.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.IdentityStates} />

### Interactions

An avatar that opens a profile card or menu needs hover and focus states like a button. A purely decorative avatar has no hover styling, so it doesn't look clickable.

## Related

- [Badge](?path=/docs/components-badge--docs) — overlay a Dot or Numeric badge on an avatar for notifications. Keep it distinct from a presence dot, which signals identity state rather than action required.

# Style

## Color

<DocTable
  head={['AvatarGlyph · Type · Color', 'Background', 'Content']}
  rows={[...[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((c) => [`Text · ${c}`, `avatar/bg/${c}`, 'text/inverse']), ['Icon', 'avatar/bg/icon', 'icon/inverse'], ['Image', 'Image fill', '—']]}
/>

<DocTable
  head={['AvatarIdentity · State', 'Background', 'Name', 'Email', 'Focus ring']}
  rows={[
    ['Default', '—', 'text/primary', 'text/secondary', '—'],
    ['Hover', 'surface/bg/subtle', 'text/primary', 'text/secondary', '—'],
    ['Focused', '—', 'text/primary', 'text/secondary', 'border/interactive/focus (3px)'],
    ['Active', 'interactive/bg/secondary/pressed', 'text/primary', 'text/secondary', '—'],
    ['Selected', 'interactive/bg/activated', 'text/primary', 'text/secondary', '—'],
    ['Disabled', '—', 'text/disabled', 'text/disabled', '—'],
  ]}
/>

## Typography

<DocTable head={['Element', 'Tokens', 'Rendered size']} plain={[2]} rows={[['Initials (Md)', 'text-style/label/md/*', '12px'], ['Name', 'text-style/label/md/*', '12px'], ['Email', 'text-style/caption/md/*', '12px']]} />

## Structure

<DocTable
  head={['Property', 'Value']}
  rows={[['Glyph size', 'size/avatar/sm · 24 · md · 32 · lg · 40'], ['Glyph shape', 'radius/full (circle)'], ['Icon', 'Icon/user/profile/20 · 20px'], ['Identity padding', 'space/inset/xs · 4'], ['Identity gap', 'space/inline/sm · 8'], ['Identity radius', 'radius/md · 6']]}
/>

## Variants & states

AvatarGlyph — 21 variants: Text Color (5) × Size (3); Icon and Image at Color 1 × Size (3). AvatarIdentity — 6 states.

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focused state with a 3px ring on AvatarIdentity.
- Hover, Active, Selected and Disabled states for interactive avatars.
- Sizes of 24, 32 and 40px — the smallest meets the 24×24px AA target minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).

## Development considerations

- Image avatars need alt text that names the person — not "avatar" or "user photo".
- Icon and initials avatars need an accessible name (`aria-label`); two letters alone aren't enough context.
- Interactive avatars need hover and focus states like a button; decorative avatars have none.

## Keyboard interactions

<Meta of={BadgeStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A badge is a small element that communicates a status, a count, a label or a notification on another element.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Default} />

<Controls of={BadgeStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Overview

A badge annotates another element with a status, a count or a short label. It never stands alone as a primary control.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Types} />

Each status color maps to exactly one meaning and is never reused for another.

### When to use

- To show the status of an item — success, warning, error, info or neutral.
- To show a count, such as unread notifications — Numeric.
- To show that something needs attention without a count — Dot.
- To tag an item with a short label — Text; a dismissible badge lets users remove it.

### When not to use

- As a primary action, button or main navigation target — use a [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs).
- For more than a short label, a single count or one icon — no paragraphs, multiple icons or nested badges.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Container** — the pill-shaped container that wraps all content.
2. **Icon** (optional) — leading and vertically centred with the label; text badges only.
3. **Label** — text or a number; omitted on dot badges.
4. **Dismiss** (optional) — trailing close control, shown only when the badge is dismissible; text badges only.

### Sizes

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Sizes} />

### Alignment

Content is centred in the container. The icon is always leading and vertically centred with the label, with a fixed gap (`space/inline/xs`).

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.IconAndDismiss} />

### Placement

Place a badge next to or on the element it describes. Content must never overflow, break or expand the parent layout.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.DoDont} />

## Content

**Label** — a short label or a single count — nothing longer.

**Count**

- If the count is above max-count (default 99), show `{max-count}+`.
- A count of 0 doesn't render unless explicitly forced.
- Dot badges ignore the count and label.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Counts} />

**Overflow content** — Text badges truncate with an ellipsis at their maximum width and never wrap to a second line.

## Behaviors

### States

Badges are static by default and have no hover, focus or disabled states.

### Interactions

A dismissible badge's close control is separately focusable and emits a dismiss event.

<DocTable head={['Key', 'Action']} rows={[['Tab', 'Moves focus to the dismiss control (dismissible badges only)']]} plain={[1]} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Dismiss} />

## Related

- [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) — use for actions; a badge must never act as a primary action.

# Style

## Color

Each Status × Style pair binds a semantic surface, text and border token.

<DocTable head={['Status · Style', 'Fill', 'Label', 'Border']} rows={COLOR_ROWS} />

Dot badges use the same fill (Filled, Subtle) or border (Outlined) tokens.

## Typography

<DocTable
  head={['Size', 'Tokens', 'Rendered size']}
  plain={[2]}
  rows={[
    ['Sm', 'text-style/caption/sm/*', '11px'],
    ['Md', 'text-style/caption/md/*', '12px'],
    ['Lg', 'text-style/label/sm/*', '11px'],
  ]}
/>

## Structure

<DocTable
  head={['Size', 'Height', 'Horizontal padding', 'Icon gap', 'Radius', 'Dot']}
  plain={[1, 5]}
  rows={[
    ['Sm', '24', 'space/inline/xs · 4', 'space/inline/xs', 'radius/full', '6 × 6'],
    ['Md', '26', 'space/inline/sm · 8', 'space/inline/xs', 'radius/full', '8 × 8'],
    ['Lg', '24', 'space/inline/md · 12', 'space/inline/xs', 'radius/full', '10 × 10'],
  ]}
/>

## Variants & states

135 variants: Status (5) × Style (3) × Type (3) × Size (3). No interactive states — badges are static.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.StatusesAndStyles} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.TypesAndStatuses} />

## Icons

The leading icon (default `Icon/feedback/star`) and dismiss icon (`Icon/action/close`) render at 12px at Size=Md. Turn them on with Has leading icon and Is dismissible.

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- Static badges have no focusable states, so they never add stray tab stops.
- Each status color maps to one meaning.
- Text badges carry their meaning in the label, not in color alone.

## Development considerations

- A static badge is not interactive — don't give it a button role.
- Dot badges have no text: expose the status they signal on the element they annotate, so meaning never relies on color alone.
- The dismiss control needs its own accessible name and must be separately focusable.

## Keyboard interactions

  rows={[
    ['Tab', 'Moves focus to the dismiss control (dismissible badges only)'],
    ['Shift + Tab', 'Moves focus to the previous focusable element'],

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocTable } from '../../storybook/helpers';
import * as BreadcrumbStories from './Breadcrumb.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ breadcrumb" — Documentation / Usage · Style · Accessibility + Example frames. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/breadcrumb-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={BreadcrumbStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A breadcrumb shows where the current page sits in a content hierarchy and links back to each parent level.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.Default} />

<Controls of={BreadcrumbStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Overview

Breadcrumbs are secondary navigation. They show the user's current position in a hierarchy and give one-click access to every ancestor level.

### Variants

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.Truncated} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.IconBased} />

### When to use

- To show the user's position within a content hierarchy.
- To give quick, one-click navigation back to parent levels.

### When not to use

- As the primary navigation of the app.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Item (link)** — a clickable ancestor level.
2. **Separator** — a decorative divider between items (chevron or slash).
3. **Collapse trigger** (optional) — an ellipsis that reveals hidden middle items.
4. **Current page** — the final item; the active location, not interactive.

### Alignment

Items and separators sit on one horizontal line, with equal spacing around each separator. Use one separator style for the whole trail.

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.Separators} />

### Placement

The trail never wraps and never causes horizontal page scroll. On small screens, collapse it to the root and the current page.

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.SmallScreens} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.DoDont} />

## Content

**Item labels**

- Each item except the last names and links to its parent level.
- Long labels truncate with an ellipsis; the full label stays available in a tooltip.

**Current page** — the final item names the page the user is on.

**Overflow content** — When the trail has more items than maxItems, the middle items collapse behind the ellipsis trigger. The root and the current page always stay visible.

## Behaviors

### States

- **Link** — Default, Hover (underline), Focused (3px focus ring) and Disabled (rare: an ancestor with no valid target).
- **Current** — Default only; never interactive.
- **Collapse trigger** — Default, Hover and Focused.
- **Separators** have no states.

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.DisabledLink} />

### Interactions

**Mouse** — Clicking a link goes to that level. Clicking the collapse trigger reveals the hidden items. The current page and separators do nothing.

<DocTable
  head={['Key', 'Action']}
  plain={[1]}
  rows={[
    ['Tab', 'Moves focus to the next link, left to right'],
    ['Enter', 'Opens the collapse trigger'],
    ['Space', 'Opens the collapse trigger'],
  ]}
/>

The current page and separators are skipped.

# Style

## Color

<DocTable
  head={['Type · State', 'Label', 'Icon', 'Focus ring']}
  rows={[
    ['Link · Default', 'text/link', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['Link · Hover', 'text/link + underline', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['Link · Focused', 'text/link + underline', 'icon/default', 'border/interactive/focus (3px)'],
    ['Link · Disabled', 'text/disabled', '—', '—'],
    ['Current · Default', 'text/primary', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['Collapse · Default', '—', 'icon/subtle', '—'],
    ['Collapse · Hover', '—', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['Collapse · Focused', '—', 'icon/default', 'border/interactive/focus (3px)'],
    ['Separator · Slash', 'text/secondary', '—', '—'],
    ['Separator · Chevron', '—', 'icon/subtle', '—'],
  ]}
/>

## Typography

<DocTable head={['Element', 'Tokens', 'Rendered size']} plain={[2]} rows={[['Item label and slash', 'text-style/label/sm/{family, weight, size}', '11px']]} />

## Structure

<DocTable
  head={['Property', 'Value']}
  rows={[
    ['Item height', '24'],
    ['Item padding', 'space/inset/xs · 4'],
    ['Icon–label gap', 'space/inline/xs'],
    ['Focus ring radius', 'radius/sm'],
    ['Leading icon', 'Icon/nav/home/16 · 16px'],
    ['Separator', 'Slash 5 × 16 · Chevron 16 × 16'],
  ]}
/>

## Variants & states

BreadcrumbItem has 8 variants: Link (Default, Hover, Focused, Disabled), Current (Default) and Collapse (Default, Hover, Focused). Separator has 2 (Slash, Chevron).

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focused state with a 3px ring on links and the collapse trigger.
- Hover adds an underline, so the link affordance doesn't rely on color alone.
- The current page is styled differently from links (`text/primary`, no underline).
- Items are 24px tall — meeting the 24×24px AA target minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).

## Development considerations

- Wrap the trail in a `<nav>` landmark with `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`, containing an ordered list (`<ol>`).
- Each ancestor is an `<a>` inside an `<li>`.
- The current page is not a link and carries `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators are decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`, not focusable, not clickable.
- The collapse trigger is keyboard-operable and reveals the hidden items.
- Truncated labels keep their full text available via a title or tooltip.

## Keyboard interactions

<DocTable
  head={['Key', 'Action']}
  plain={[1]}
  rows={[
    ['Tab', 'Moves focus to the next link, left to right'],
    ['Shift + Tab', 'Moves focus to the previous link'],
    ['Enter', 'Opens the collapse trigger'],
    ['Space', 'Opens the collapse trigger'],
  ]}
/>

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbStories.Keyboard} />

Items and the collapse trigger are 24px tall, meeting the AA minimum but below the 44×44px touch target in the component rules — pad the hit area on touch screens.

Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/button-story-skill.md. */} export const Table = ({ head, rows }) => ( {head.map((h) => )}{rows.map((r, i) => {r.map((c, j) => )})}

); export const VARIANTS = ['Primary', 'Secondary', 'Ghost', 'Danger']; export const STATES = ['Default', 'Hover', 'Pressed', 'Focused', 'Disabled']; export const border = (v, s) => s === 'Focused' ? 'border/interactive/focus (3px)' : v !== 'Secondary' ? '—' : s === 'Default' ? 'border/interactive/default' : s === 'Disabled' ? 'border/interactive/disabled' : 'border/interactive/hover'; export const COLOR_ROWS = VARIANTS.flatMap((v) => STATES.map((s) => { const k = `${v.toLowerCase()}/${s.toLowerCase()}`; return [`${v} · ${s}`, `interactive/bg/${k}`, `interactive/fg/${k}`, border(v, s)]; }), ); <Subtitle>A button triggers an immediate action, such as submit, confirm, open or delete.</Subtitle> <Canvas of={ButtonStories.Default} /> <Controls of={ButtonStories.Default} /> # Usage ## Overview A button triggers an immediate action in the current context — submitting a form, confirming a choice, opening something or deleting an item. Four emphasis levels (Primary, Secondary, Ghost, Danger) keep the most important action on a screen the easiest one to find. Use buttons for actions only. If activating it takes the user to another page or location, it is navigation and must not be a button. ### When to use - To let users submit, confirm, open or delete something immediately. - To mark the single most important action in a context — **Primary**. - To offer supporting actions of lower weight next to a primary one — **Secondary** or **Ghost**. - To trigger destructive or irreversible actions such as delete or remove — **Danger**. ### When not to use - When the action navigates to another page or location — use a text link instead. - Don't use Danger styling for actions that aren't destructive — use Primary, Secondary or Ghost. ## Formatting ### Anatomy 1. **Container** — the interactive wrapper; owns variant, size and state. 2. **Icon** (optional) — leading or trailing, never both. Vertically centred with the label. Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology. 3. **Label** — text describing the action. Required unless the button is icon-only. ### Sizes Every variant shares the same size scale. Each size defines its own height, horizontal padding, font size and icon size. <Canvas of={ButtonStories.Sizes} /> ### Alignment Content is always centred horizontally and vertically. The icon sits on the side set by the icon property and is vertically centred with the label; the icon–label gap is the same across variants. <Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIcons} /> ### Placement Buttons hug their content within the size's padding and are not stretched. <Canvas of={ButtonStories.DoDont} /> ## Content **Label** - Use a verb that describes the action, e.g. Save, Delete, Open. - Required on every button unless it is icon-only. **Icon** - Optional — leading or trailing, never both. - Decorative icons must be hidden from assistive technology. - Icon-only buttons must have an accessible label (`aria-label`). ## Behaviors ### States A button has no persistent on/off state: it runs its action and returns to rest. Every variant starts in the Default state. - **Default** — resting. - **Hover** — the pointer is over the button. - **Pressed** — during a press; gives immediate visual feedback so the press registers. - **Focused** — keyboard focus; always shows a visible focus indicator. - **Disabled** — non-interactive, with reduced emphasis. ### Interactions **Mouse** — Clicking anywhere on the button runs its action. Disabled buttons ignore clicks. **Keyboard** <Table head={['Key', 'Action']} rows={[['Tab', 'Moves focus to the button'], ['Enter', 'Activates the button'], ['Space', 'Activates the button']]} /> # Style ## Color Each variant and state maps to a semantic interactive token. <Table head={['Variant · State', 'Background', 'Label', 'Border']} rows={COLOR_ROWS} /> ## Typography The label binds all five typography properties (family, weight, size, line height in px, letter spacing) to the label text-style tokens for its size. <Table head={['Size', 'Tokens', 'Rendered size']} rows={[ ['Sm', 'text-style/label/sm/{family, weight, size, line-height-px, letter-spacing}', '11px'], ['Md', 'text-style/label/md/{family, weight, size, line-height-px, letter-spacing}', '12px'], ['Lg', 'text-style/label/lg/{family, weight, size, line-height-px, letter-spacing}', '14px'], ]} /> ## Structure <Table head={['Size', 'Min height', 'Horizontal padding', 'Icon–label gap', 'Radius']} rows={[ ['Sm', 'size/control/sm · 32', 'space/inline/md · 12', 'space/inline/sm · 8', 'radius/control · 6'], ['Md', 'size/control/md · 40', 'space/inline/lg · 16', 'space/inline/sm · 8', 'radius/control · 6'], ['Lg', 'size/control/lg · 48', 'space/inline/xl · 24', 'space/inline/sm · 8', 'radius/control · 6'], ]} /> ### Radius <Canvas of={ButtonStories.Radius} /> ## Variants & states 180 variants: Variant (4) × Size (3) × State (5) × Radius (3). The grid shows Variant × State at Size=Md, Radius=Default. <Canvas of={ButtonStories.VariantsAndStates} /> ### Focus Every variant's Focused state adds a 3px ring bound to `border/interactive/focus`. <Canvas of={ButtonStories.Focused} /> ## Icons Leading and trailing icon slots are 20px at Size=Md, with width bound to an icon size token. Turn them on with Has leading icon / Has trailing icon. # Accessibility ## What the design system provides - A Focused state on every variant, with a 3px ring bound to `border/interactive/focus`. - A Disabled state on every variant. - Label typography bound to all five label text-style tokens for each size. - Minimum heights of 32, 40 and 48px — all above the 24×24px target-size minimum (WCAG 2.5.8). ## Development considerations - Use a native `<button>` element. Default to `type="button"` to avoid accidental form submits; use `submit` or `reset` only when intended. - Disabled: use the `disabled` attribute or `aria-disabled="true"`. Disabled buttons must block clicks, keypresses and focus-triggered actions. - Icon-only buttons need an accessible name via `aria-label`. - Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`. - Never convey state through color alone. ## Keyboard interactions <Table head={['Key', 'Action']} rows={[ ['Tab', 'Moves focus to the next focusable element'], ['Shift + Tab', 'Moves focus to the previous focusable element'], ['Enter', 'Activates the button'], ['Space', 'Activates the button'], ]} /> Keyboard focus must always be visible. Pointer focus may hide the ring (focus-visible only). <Canvas of={ButtonStories.KeyboardActivation} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocTable } from '../../storybook/helpers';
import * as CarouselStories from './Carousel.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ carousel" — Documentation / Usage · Style · Accessibility + Example frames. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/carousel-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={CarouselStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A carousel shows a set of items one view at a time inside a fixed viewport, advanced with controls, swipe or autoplay.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Standard} />

<Controls of={CarouselStories.Standard} />

# Usage

## Overview

A carousel shows a subset of items at once when they exceed the available space. It's assembled from three components — NavControl, PaginationDot and AutoplayToggle — around the viewport and slides.

### Variants

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Standard} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Autoplay} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.MultiItem} />

Behavior options: infinite (wraps from last to first) or finite (stops at the edges); single-item or multi-item; slide or fade transition.

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Infinite} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Fade} />

### When to use

- When items exceed the available space and only a subset should be visible at once.

### When not to use

- For content users need to compare side by side.
- For content users need to read in full.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Container** — the root; owns state and bounds.
2. **Navigation controls** — Prev and Next NavControl buttons.
3. **Viewport** — clips overflow and shows the current slide.
4. **Pagination** — PaginationDots showing position and count; the active dot is larger.

### Alignment and placement

All slides share identical dimensions within a breakpoint. The gap between slides is consistent, and the first and last slides align flush to the viewport edges. Reserve the viewport height up front so loading media doesn't shift the layout. Don't nest a horizontal carousel inside another on the same axis.

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.DoDont} />

## Content

- **Slides** — every slide in a breakpoint has the same size; off-screen slides are inert, not reachable by Tab.
- **Pagination** — dots show position and count; the active dot is larger.
- **Autoplay interval** — at least 4000ms (default 5000ms) so content stays readable.

## Behaviors

### States

- **Active slide** — its pagination dot is marked current.
- **Disabled navigation** — in finite mode, Prev or Next disables at the edges.
- **Hover** — controls become more prominent and autoplay pauses.
- **Focus** — visible 3px focus ring on the focused control.
- **Autoplay** — Playing or Paused.

### Interactions

Prev and Next advance by one slide, or one page when several slides are in view, and the pagination updates with the slide. Autoplay advances on the interval and pauses on hover, when focus is inside the carousel and when the tab is hidden. It stops for good once the user interacts with any control.

# Style

## Color

<DocTable
  head={['Component · State', 'Fill', 'Icon', 'Focus ring']}
  rows={[
    ['NavControl · Default', 'surface/bg/elevated', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['NavControl · Hover', 'surface/bg/subtle', 'icon/default', '—'],
    ['NavControl · Focused', 'surface/bg/elevated', 'icon/default', 'border/interactive/focus (3px)'],
    ['NavControl · Disabled', 'surface/bg/elevated', 'icon/subtle', '—'],
    ['PaginationDot · Default', 'border/strong', '—', '—'],
    ['PaginationDot · Active', 'interactive/bg/primary/default', '—', '—'],
    ['AutoplayToggle · Playing', 'surface/bg/elevated', 'icon/default (pause)', '—'],
    ['AutoplayToggle · Paused', 'surface/bg/elevated', 'icon/default (play)', '—'],
  ]}
/>

## Structure

<DocTable
  head={['Component', 'Size', 'Radius', 'Icon']}
  plain={[1]}
  rows={[
    ['NavControl', '36 × 36', 'radius/full', 'Icon/nav/chevron-left|right/20'],
    ['AutoplayToggle', '32 × 32', 'radius/full', 'Icon/media/pause|play/16'],
    ['PaginationDot · Default', '8 × 8', 'radius/full', '—'],
    ['PaginationDot · Active', '10 × 10', 'radius/full', '—'],
  ]}
/>

## Variants & states

NavControl — 8 variants: Direction (Prev, Next) × State (Default, Hover, Focused, Disabled). PaginationDot and AutoplayToggle — 2 variants each.

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focused state with a 3px ring on NavControl.
- A Disabled NavControl state for the edges of finite carousels.
- An AutoplayToggle with Playing and Paused states, so autoplay can always be stopped.

## Development considerations

- Wrap the slides in a live region (`aria-live="polite"`), turned off during autoplay, so slide changes are announced.
- Make off-screen slides inert so they can't be reached by Tab.
- Don't move focus when the slide changes unless the user triggered it by keyboard.
- Pagination dots must be reachable and operable by keyboard.
- Prev, Next, pause and dot controls are icon-only — each needs an accessible name.
- Pause autoplay on hover, focus-within and a hidden tab; stop it after any interaction.

## Keyboard interactions

<DocTable
  head={['Key', 'Action']}
  plain={[1]}
  rows={[['← →', 'Move to the previous or next slide'], ['Home', 'Jump to the first slide'], ['End', 'Jump to the last slide'], ['Tab', 'Move through the controls, including pagination dots']]}
/>

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Keyboard} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocTable } from '../../storybook/helpers';
import * as CheckboxStories from './Checkbox.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ checkbox" — Documentation / Usage · Style · Accessibility. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/checkbox-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={CheckboxStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A checkbox is a square control that users select or clear — used on its own, as a labeled field, or as a titled group of fields.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Default} />

<Controls of={CheckboxStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Overview

Checkbox is built as three layered components, from atom to organism:

- **CheckboxControl** — the box alone: border, fill, focus ring and check or dash icon. No label.
- **CheckboxField** — label, control, value text, and optional description, helper and error or warning messages.
- **CheckboxGroup** — a group label with CheckboxFields, vertical or horizontal.

### Selection types

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.SelectionTypes} />

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Label** — the field label (Has label).
2. **Description** (optional) — text below the label (Has description).
3. **Control** — a CheckboxControl: box, border, focus ring, check or dash icon.
4. **Value** — the checkbox's own text, describing what checking it means.
5. **Error or warning message** — icon and text, shown in the Invalid and Warning states.
6. **Helper text** (optional) — supporting text below the field (Has helper).

### Sizes

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Sizes} />

### Alignment

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Group} />

## Content

- **Label** — the field or group title.
- **Value** — the checkbox's own text; describes what checking it means.
- **Description and helper text** — optional supporting text; description sits under the label, helper text under the field.
- **Error and warning messages** — shown as text with a status icon, so validation never relies on color alone.
- **Overflow** — label and value text wrap.

## Behaviors

### States

Each field has a selection type — Unselected, Selected or Indeterminate — and a field state. Invalid switches the control to its Error type.

- **Enabled** — resting.
- **Focus** — keyboard focus; the control shows a 3px focus ring (`border/interactive/focus`).
- **Invalid** — error border and an error message.
- **Warning** — a warning message.
- **Read-only** — value text is dimmed and the value can't be changed.
- **Disabled** — label, value and box are dimmed; the field is non-interactive.
- **Skeleton** — placeholder shapes while content loads.

CheckboxControl adds Hovered and Pressed pointer states.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.FieldStates} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.GroupStates} />

## Related

- [List item](?path=/docs/components-list-item--docs) — uses CheckboxControl as its leading or trailing control for multi-select lists.

# Style

## Color

CheckboxControl box fill and border per type and state (Size=Md).

<DocTable
  head={['Type · State', 'Box fill', 'Border']}
  rows={[
    ['Unselected · Enabled', 'surface/bg/default', 'border/interactive/default'],
    ['Unselected · Hovered / Pressed', 'surface/bg/default', 'border/interactive/hover'],
    ['Unselected · Focused', 'surface/bg/default', 'border/interactive/focus'],
    ['Unselected · Disabled', 'surface/bg/subtle', 'border/interactive/disabled'],
    ['Selected / Indeterminate · Enabled, Focused', 'interactive/bg/primary/default', 'interactive/bg/primary/default'],
    ['Selected / Indeterminate · Hovered', 'interactive/bg/primary/hover', 'interactive/bg/primary/hover'],
    ['Selected / Indeterminate · Pressed', 'interactive/bg/primary/pressed', 'interactive/bg/primary/pressed'],
    ['Selected / Indeterminate · Disabled', 'interactive/bg/primary/disabled', 'interactive/bg/primary/disabled'],
    ['Error-Unselected · Enabled → Focused', 'surface/bg/default', 'border/interactive/error'],
    ['Error-Selected · Enabled, Focused', 'interactive/bg/danger/default', 'border/interactive/error'],
    ['Error-Selected · Hovered', 'interactive/bg/danger/hover', 'border/interactive/error'],
    ['Error-Selected · Pressed', 'interactive/bg/danger/pressed', 'border/interactive/error'],
    ['Error-* · Disabled', 'surface/bg/subtle or interactive/bg/danger/disabled', 'border/interactive/disabled'],
  ]}
/>

## Variants & states

CheckboxControl: Size (3) × Type (6) × State (5) — 90 variants. CheckboxField: Type (3) × State (6) — 18. CheckboxGroup: State (4) × Orientation (2) — 8.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.ControlTypesAndStates} />

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focus state with a 3px ring outside the box, on every type.
- An Indeterminate type for mixed selection.
- Error and warning messages as text with an icon, not color alone.
- Disabled and Read-only states for the field.

## Development considerations

- Use `role="checkbox"` (or a native checkbox) with `aria-checked` — `"mixed"` for Indeterminate.
- Group related checkboxes with `role="group"`, labelled by the group label.
- Set `aria-invalid` on fields in the Invalid state and associate the error message with the control.
- Disabled checkboxes must not receive keyboard focus.
- Make the value text part of the clickable area — the box alone is 16–24px.

## Keyboard interactions

<DocTable head={['Key', 'Action']} plain={[1]} rows={[['Tab', 'Moves focus to the next checkbox'], ['Shift + Tab', 'Moves focus to the previous checkbox']]} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Keyboard} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as DatePickerStories from './DatePicker.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ Date Picker" — Documentation frame + Examples. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/date-picker-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={DatePickerStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A single component covering single-date, date-range and date + time selection, with the calendar panel shown on demand.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Default} />

<Controls of={DatePickerStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Anatomy

1. **Date field(s)** — every field carries a trailing calendar icon, never leading. A range field renders two side by side sharing one popover.
2. **Presets** — a side list next to the calendar.
3. **Calendar** — month grid(s) with Default, Selected, In-range and Today day cells.
4. **Footer actions** — Clear / Cancel / Apply, so a stray click never commits a half-made range selection.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.ShowCalendar} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Types} />

# Style

## Variants & states

21 variants: Type (Single / Range / DateTime) × State (Default / Hover / Focused / Filled / Disabled / Read-only / Error).

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.States} />

## Token map

`color/field/border/focused` — Single / Focused field border. The `component.date-picker` collection holds `color/field/border/{default|hover|focused|disabled|read-only|error}`, `color/field/text/error`, `color/field/icon/error`, `color/calendar/border`, and equivalents for the calendar day-cell states.

# Accessibility

- The month grid always renders 42 cells (6 full weeks) so grid height never jumps between months.
- Range selection: the first click sets the start, the second sets the end, a third click starts a new range; clicking before the current start moves the start instead of erroring.
- Arrow keys move focus day-to-day (← → ±1, ↑ ↓ ±7); Enter / Space selects; Escape closes without committing.
- Each day announces weekday, full date and active state to assistive tech.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Keyboard} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as DividerStories from './Divider.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ divider" — Documentation frame. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/divider-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={DividerStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A rule line with five variant axes — Orientation, Style, Size, Color and State.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Default} />

<Controls of={DividerStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Anatomy

1. **Line** — a single line rendered with a stroke, for every Style value.

The root hugs both axes at the Size-driven length (Sm = 24px, Md = 48px) and carries no fill of its own.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Orientation} />

# Style

## Variants & states

540 variants: Orientation (2) × Style (3) × Size (2) × Color (9) × State (5). The grid is a representative subset: Color × Style at Orientation=Horizontal, Size=Md, State=Default. A mid-grey backdrop is used because Light, Subtle and Transparent are intentionally pale.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.ColorsAndStyles} />

### State

Focused and Selected render at the strong stroke width (2px); Default, Hover and Disabled render at 1px.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.States} />

## Token map

`color/dark` — Color=Dark stroke colour. The `component.divider` collection holds 9 colour variables (each aliasing a semantic border token), 9 colour-opacity values (only Transparent is 0), 5 state stroke widths (Focused / Selected alias the 2px "strong" width, the rest 1px "default"), 5 state opacities (only Disabled is 40) and 2 hug lengths (Sm 24px, Md 48px).

# Accessibility

The divider itself is not clickable — State is a visual signal set by the consumer, not user interaction. A List Item or Tabs component might use State=Selected or Focused to draw a heavier, tinted line next to an active row.

Decorative: use `role="separator"` when the divider is semantically meaningful, otherwise `aria-hidden="true"`.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Semantics} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as IconStories from './Icon.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ Icons" — Documentation frame + icons variable collection. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/icon-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={IconStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>Every icon used across the system as its own component (Icon/semantic/size), reused by every consuming component — never hand-drawn inside a component.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={IconStories.Default} />

<Controls of={IconStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Anatomy

1. **Icon vector** — stroke-only (no fill), round caps and joins, stroke weight bound to `icon/stroke/{size}`.

## Representative icons

The semantic icons span 8 categories (action, nav, form, status, media, layout, user, feedback). The grid shows one icon per category at all 3 built sizes.

<Canvas of={IconStories.Representative} />

<Canvas of={IconStories.Gallery} />

# Style

## Sizes

Built at 16, 20 and 24px.

<Canvas of={IconStories.Sizes} />

## Token map

`icon/color/default` — default stroke colour. Size: `icon/size/{sm|md|lg}`. Stroke weight: `icon/stroke/{sm|md|lg}`. Consuming components override the instance stroke colour with their own component-level token (e.g. `component/checkbox/color/icon/error`) rather than using `icon/color/default` directly.

<Canvas of={IconStories.Colors} />

# Accessibility

Icons are decorative by default (`aria-hidden="true"`). Meaningful icons (icon-only buttons, status icons that carry information) must have an `aria-label` set by the consuming component — the Icon itself carries no accessible name. Disabled state is opacity applied by the consumer, not a dedicated icon variant.

<Canvas of={IconStories.Meaningful} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocTable } from '../../storybook/helpers';
import * as ListItemStories from './ListItem.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ list-item" — Documentation / Usage · Style · Accessibility + Examples. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/list-item-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={ListItemStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A list item is a single row in a list, menu or file browser that shows a headline and, depending on its type, an icon, supporting text, metadata or a selection control.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={ListItemStories.Default} />

<Controls of={ListItemStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Overview

List items are the rows that make up a list. Each type has a fixed set of content, so choose the type that matches what the row represents. Any type can also hold a Checkbox or Radio at its start or end, for multi-select or single-select lists.

<Canvas of={ListItemStories.Types} />

### When to use

- To show a vertical set of related items — Default.
- To list actions or destinations in a menu — Menu.
- To show files with an icon, details and metadata — File.
- To show a setting with a short description — Setting.
- To let users pick one or several items — add a Radio or Checkbox as a leading or trailing control.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Container** — the row's visual container; carries state colors, padding and radius.
2. **Leading icon** — File and Setting types only.
3. **Headline** — required title text, on every type.
4. **Supporting text** — File and Setting types only.
5. **Metadata** — trailing text such as a count or file size; File type only.

### Sizes

Each size has its own minimum height, padding, gap, icon size and type size.

<Canvas of={ListItemStories.Sizes} />

### Alignment

<Canvas of={ListItemStories.Controls} />

<Canvas of={ListItemStories.DoDont} />

## Content

- **Headline** — required on every type and always visible.
- **Supporting text** — secondary detail under the headline; File and Setting types.
- **Metadata** — short trailing text such as a timestamp, size or count; File type.

## Behaviors

### States

Items start unselected (Default). Selected is a persistent highlight for chosen items; Activated is a persistent indicator for the current navigation location. Both are token swaps on the container.

- **Hover and Pressed** — pointer feedback.
- **Focused** — keyboard focus, shown with a 2px border (`color/border/focused`).
- **Disabled** — non-interactive.
- **Dragged** — the item is being moved; 2px border (`color/border/dragged`).
- **Skeleton** — placeholder shapes while content loads.

<Canvas of={ListItemStories.States} />

### Interactions

**Mouse** — hovering and pressing a row show the Hover and Pressed states. A leading or trailing control is a real Checkbox or Radio and keeps its own interaction.

## Related

- [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) — the box used as a leading or trailing control in multi-select lists.
- [Radio](?path=/docs/components-radio--docs) — the radio circle used as a control in single-select lists.

# Style

## Color

Each state aliases its own `component.list-item` token.

<DocTable
  head={['State', 'Background', 'Headline', 'Supporting text', 'Border']}
  rows={['default', 'hover', 'pressed', 'focused', 'disabled', 'selected', 'activated', 'dragged'].map((s) => [
    s[0].toUpperCase() + s.slice(1),
    `color/bg/${s}`,
    `color/label/${s}`,
    `color/supporting-text/${s}`,
    s === 'focused' || s === 'dragged' ? `color/border/${s} (2px)` : '—',
  ])}
/>

Icon color follows the same pattern: `color/icon/{state}`.

## Typography

<DocTable head={['Size', 'Headline', 'Supporting text · metadata']} plain={[1, 2]} rows={[['Sm', '12px', '11px'], ['Md', '13px', '12px'], ['Lg', '14px', '13px']]} />

## Structure

<DocTable
  head={['Size', 'Min height', 'Padding', 'Gap', 'Radius', 'Leading icon']}
  rows={[
    ['Sm', 'size/height/sm · 32', 'space/padding/sm · 8', 'space/gap/sm · 4', 'radius · 6', 'icon/size/sm · 16'],
    ['Md', 'size/height/md · 40', 'space/padding/md · 12', 'space/gap/md · 8', 'radius · 6', 'icon/size/md · 20'],
    ['Lg', 'size/height/lg · 48', 'space/padding/lg · 16', 'space/gap/lg · 8', 'radius · 6', 'icon/size/lg · 24'],
  ]}
/>

## Variants & states

108 variants: Type (4) × State (9) × Size (3).

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focused state on every type, with a 2px border bound to `color/border/focused`.
- Disabled, Selected, Activated, Dragged and Skeleton states, each a token swap on the container.
- Selection controls are real Checkbox / Radio instances, so they inherit those components' accessibility.
- Minimum heights of 32, 40 and 48px — above the 24×24px target-size minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).

## Development considerations

- Use `role="list"` on the container and `role="listitem"` on each item.
- Expose selection with `aria-selected`.
- Dragging must have a non-drag alternative.

## Keyboard interactions

<DocTable head={['Key', 'Action']} plain={[1]} rows={[['↑ ↓', 'Move between items at the same level'], ['Tab', 'Move between interactive elements']]} />

<Canvas of={ListItemStories.Keyboard} />

import { Meta, Title, Subtitle, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocTable } from '../../storybook/helpers';
import * as DialogStories from './Modal.stories';

{/* Source: Figma "↳ dialog" — Documentation / Usage · Style · Accessibility + Examples. Generated per agents/08-storybook-agent/dialog-story-skill.md. */}

<Meta of={DialogStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A dialog is a focused window layered over the page that blocks interaction until a task or decision is resolved.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Confirmation} />

<Controls of={DialogStories.Confirmation} />

# Usage

## Overview

A dialog interrupts the page to focus the user on exactly one task or decision. It's the most disruptive surface available — it blocks everything else until it's resolved — so use it sparingly.

### Types

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Alert} />

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Form} />

<Canvas of={DialogStories.FullScreen} />

<Canvas of={DialogStories.SideDrawer} />

### Footer patterns

<DocTable
  head={['Pattern', 'Purpose', 'Footer']}
  plain={[1, 2]}
  rows={[
    ['Passive', 'Information to be aware of; no decision', 'No action buttons — dismiss only'],
    ['Transactional', 'An action is needed to complete and close', 'Cancel + one primary action'],
    ['Danger', 'A destructive or irreversible action', 'Cancel + a danger-styled primary action'],
    ['Acknowledgment', 'The user must actively acknowledge something', 'A single button (commonly OK)'],
    ['Progress', 'A task in several steps', 'Cancel + Previous + Next (or the completing action on the last step)'],
  ]}
/>

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Danger} />

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Passive} />

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Progress} />

### When to use

- To get an immediate response needed to continue something the user just started.
- To notify the user of urgent information tied to their current work.
- To confirm a decision — especially a destructive or irreversible one.

### When not to use

- For information that isn't urgent — use an inline [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) instead.
- For tasks users repeat often — let them complete it on the page.
- When even the largest size isn't enough room — use a full page.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Title** — a short, specific verb phrase naming the task.
2. **Subtitle** (optional) — short context for the title (Has subtitle).
3. **Close icon** — always available for dismissal.
4. **Body** — message text and/or embedded content such as form fields.
5. **Secondary action** — e.g. Cancel, on the left.
6. **Primary action** — the one action that completes the task, on the right.

### Sizes

Small · 400px, Medium · 480px, Large · 640px. Choose the size by content: brief text fits Small; complex embedded content needs Medium or Large. If content keeps scrolling, move up a size; if the largest isn't enough, use a full page.

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Sizes} />

### Placement

Center the dialog vertically for short, predictable content, or pin it at a fixed offset from the top for longer or variable content. Use a dimmed backdrop by default. Clicking the backdrop may close passive dialogs, but never transactional or destructive ones. Avoid opening a dialog from inside another dialog.

### Do and don't

- **Do** — secondary (Cancel) on the left, primary on the right — one clear emphasis. **Don't** use two primary buttons — the user can't tell which action is safe.
- **Do** — for destructive actions, name the action in the title and use a danger-styled, specific button. **Don't** use vague titles or buttons like OK for a destructive action.

## Content

- **Title** — a short, specific verb phrase that matches whatever opened the dialog. For a very short message, let the title carry it and skip the body.
- **Subtitle** — only when the purpose isn't obvious from the title.
- **Body** — brief; only the fields and content needed to complete the task.
- **Buttons** — short, specific verbs (Delete, Save, Add), not vague labels like Done. OK is fine only for the acknowledgment pattern.
- **Overflow** — when the body needs to scroll, the header and footer stay fixed and only the body scrolls. Content never scrolls horizontally — move up a size instead.

<Canvas of={DialogStories.ScrollableContent} />

## Behaviors

### States

- **Open** — ready for input.
- **Loading** — the footer buttons are disabled while the action runs, preventing a double submit.
- **Error** — Form only: an error banner at the top of the body, with the fields to correct.

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Loading} />

<Canvas of={DialogStories.FormError} />

### Interactions

- Opens only as the direct result of a user action — never unprompted.
- Initial focus lands on the first form field, or on the primary button if there's no form.
- Focus stays inside the dialog while it's open; on close it returns to the trigger.
- Close with the close icon, Escape, or — for passive dialogs only — a click outside. Cancel reverts any staged changes.
- Validate before closing on submit; keep the dialog open and mark fields in error.
- Background page scroll is locked while the dialog is open.

## Related

- [Alert](?path=/docs/components-alert--docs) — for inline, non-urgent feedback that shouldn't interrupt the page.
- [Button](?path=/docs/components-button--docs) — used for the footer actions.

## Color

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A close icon on every type, alongside Escape.
- Footer actions are real Buttons, with their focus and disabled states.
- A Loading state that disables the footer buttons to prevent double submits.
- A Form Error state with a text error banner, not color alone.

## Development considerations

- Use `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the title.
- Trap focus inside the dialog; return focus to the trigger on close.
- Exclude background content from the accessibility tree while a decision is required — not just dim it.
- The close icon is icon-only — give it an accessible name.
- Set initial focus on the first field, or the primary button when there's no form.

<Meta of={RadioStories} />

<Title />

<Subtitle>A radio button lets users pick exactly one option from a set — shown on its own, as a labeled field, or in a titled group.</Subtitle>

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Default} />

<Controls of={RadioStories.Default} />

# Usage

## Overview

Radio is built as three layered components, from atom to organism. Only one radio in a group can be selected at a time.

- **RadioControl** — the circle alone: outer ring and inner dot. No label.
- **RadioField** — a control with its value text and optional error or warning row.
- **RadioGroup** — a group label with RadioFields, vertical or horizontal.

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Control** — outer circle, inner dot when selected, focus ring when focused.
2. **Value** — the option's own text.
3. **Status icon** — error or warning icon, shown in the Invalid and Warning states.
4. **Message** — the error or warning text.

In a RadioGroup, a group label sits above the fields.

### Alignment

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Position} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Horizontal} />

## Content

- **Group label** — required on every RadioGroup; names the choice being made.
- **Value** — the text of each option.
- **Error and warning messages** — text with a status icon, shown in the Invalid and Warning states.

## Behaviors

### States

Selecting a radio clears the other radios in its group. Read-only only ever shows an option that's already selected — it displays a prior choice, so there is no read-only radio with nothing selected.

- **RadioControl** — Enabled, Hovered, Focused, Pressed, Disabled, Skeleton, Read-Only, Invalid, Warning; each Selected or not.
- **RadioField** — Enabled, Focused, Invalid, Warning, Read-Only, Disabled, Skeleton.
- **RadioGroup** — Enabled, Read-Only, Invalid, Warning.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.GroupStates} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.FieldStates} />

## Related

- [List item](?path=/docs/components-list-item--docs) — uses RadioControl as its control for single-select lists.
- [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-checkbox--docs) — the equivalent control for multi-select lists.

<DocTable

  rows={['enabled', 'hovered', 'focused', 'pressed', 'disabled', 'skeleton', 'read-only', 'invalid', 'warning'].map((s) => [
    s[0].toUpperCase() + s.slice(1),
    `color/control/border/${s}`,
    s === 'skeleton' ? 'color/control/border/skeleton' : `color/control/dot/${s}`,

## Variants & states

RadioControl — 17 variants: State (9) × Selected (2), minus Read-Only unselected. RadioField — 14: State (7) × Position (2). RadioGroup — 8: State (4) × Horizontal (2).

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focused state with a focus ring on the control.
- Invalid and Warning states with a text message and icon, not color alone.
- Read-Only and Disabled states.

## Development considerations

- Each option uses `role="radio"` (or a native radio) with `aria-checked`.
- Wrap the options in `role="radiogroup"`, labelled by the group label.
- Only one option in a group can be checked.
- Disabled radios must not receive keyboard focus.

<Title />

<Subtitle>A dropdown is a select control: a trigger field that opens a menu of options.</Subtitle>

# Usage

## Overview

Dropdown is built from three components: DropdownTrigger (the field), DropdownMenu (the option list, made of List item instances) and Dropdown (the two combined, collapsed or expanded).

### Patterns

These are example compositions on the Figma page, built from the trigger and menu — not variants of Dropdown.

<Canvas of={DropdownStories.Searchable} />

<Canvas of={DropdownStories.Grouped} />

<Canvas of={DropdownStories.Clearable} />

## Formatting

### Anatomy

1. **Value** — the selected option, or placeholder text.
2. **Chevron** — points down when closed and rotates 180° when open.
3. **Menu** — the option-list surface.
4. **Option** — a List item instance.

### Sizes

The trigger is 320px wide at every size; the menu opens below it at the same width.

<Canvas of={DropdownStories.Sizes} />

## Content

- **Value and placeholder** — shows the selected option, or placeholder text ("Select an option") when nothing is selected.
- **Menu messages** — Loading shows a loading message with a loading icon; Empty shows "No results found".

## Behaviors

### States

- **Trigger** — Default, Hover, Focused, Disabled, Error and Read-only (no chevron).
- **Expanded** — the trigger takes the focus border and the chevron rotates 180°.
- **Menu** — Default, Loading and Empty.

<Canvas of={DropdownStories.TriggerStates} />

<Canvas of={DropdownStories.MenuStates} />

## Related

- [List item](?path=/docs/components-list-item--docs) — each menu option is a List item instance.

# Style

## Color

<DocTable
  head={['Trigger state', 'Fill', 'Border', 'Value text']}
  rows={[

    ['Error', 'surface/bg/elevated', 'border/interactive/error', 'text/placeholder'],
    ['Read-only', 'interactive/bg/readonly', 'interactive/border/readonly', 'interactive/fg/readonly'],
  ]}
/>

The chevron uses `icon/color/default`; Read-only has no chevron. The menu uses `surface/bg/elevated`, `border/default`, and `text/secondary` for group labels and messages.

## Typography

<DocTable head={['Element', 'Token', 'Rendered size']} plain={[2]} rows={[['Trigger value', 'typography/size/md (primitive)', '14px'], ['Group label', '—', '11px']]} />

## Structure

<DocTable
  head={['Property', 'Value']}
  rows={[['Trigger height', 'size/control/sm · md · lg — 32 / 40 / 48'], ['Trigger width', '320'], ['Trigger padding', 'space/inset/sm · 8'], ['Trigger radius', 'radius/control · 6'], ['Chevron', 'Icon/nav/chevron-down/16'], ['Menu radius', 'radius/surface · 8']]}
/>

## Variants & states

DropdownTrigger — 21 variants: Size (3) × State (6) collapsed, plus one Expanded variant per size. DropdownMenu — 3 (Default, Loading, Empty). Dropdown — 6 (Size × Collapsed / Expanded).

# Accessibility

## What the design system provides

- A Focused state with a focus border on the trigger.
- Disabled, Error and Read-only trigger states.
- Loading and Empty menu states with text messages.
- Trigger heights of 32, 40 and 48px — all above the 24×24px AA target minimum (WCAG 2.5.8).

## Development considerations

- Placeholder text must not replace a visible label — pair the dropdown with a label.
- In the Error state, give a text error message, not just a red border — and set `aria-invalid`.
- Disabled dropdowns must not receive keyboard focus.
- The dropdown must be fully operable by keyboard.

# Usage

## Anatomy

1. **Track** — the pill-shaped background the handle slides within.
2. **Handle** — the circular thumb that slides from one side to the other to indicate state.
3. **Inner icon** — an Icon inside the handle, swapping between On / Off glyphs as the state changes.

## Properties & content

Two sizes: Medium (default / general use) and Small (dense contexts). Inner icon content swaps between On / Off glyphs immediately as state changes, reinforcing the resulting state at a glance rather than relying on handle position alone.

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.InnerContent} />

## Example: settings list

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.SettingsList} />

# Style

## Variants & states

12 variants: Value (Off / On) × Interaction (Default / Disabled / Loading) × Size (Medium / Small). The grid shows Value × Interaction at Size=Medium.

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.ValuesAndInteractions} />

## Token map

`color/track/bg/on` — track fill, On / Default / Medium.

# Accessibility

- Click or tap anywhere on the track toggles state, not just the handle.
- Keyboard: focusable, toggles via Space.
- Loading shows a pending indicator on the handle, distinct from Disabled.
- Implement with real switch semantics (`role="switch"`, `aria-checked`), not a generic checkbox role.
- Label by what the setting controls ("Notifications"), not by its current state.
